idea.title: Keeping documentation aligned after a folder-structure refactor
idea.summary: A renderer folder refactor had already reached main, but several architecture guides, workflow instructions, source comments, and a temporary type re-export still pointed at the old locations.

context.goal: Bring current documentation and source imports into line with the merged renderer structure without changing runtime behavior.
context.situation: The renderer now owns models, layouts, components, data fixtures, safety, and its adapter under src/renderer, while Studio and the export view have their own directories.
context.investigation: Searched current docs, source, README, and workflow guidance for former renderer and draft paths; distinguished active instructions from intentionally preserved historical idea and published records.
context.decision: Update current source-of-truth references, migrate renderer model imports directly, remove the compatibility shim, and leave historical records intact.
context.implementation: Corrected architecture and development documentation, README workflow notes, Workflow 04 draft paths, and Workflow 04 source comments; migrated the remaining Studio renderer-model imports and deleted src/types.ts.
context.result: Renderer tests and production build passed, and the diff whitespace check passed. No runtime behavior was intentionally changed.

learning_points: A folder refactor is not complete until docs, agent instructions, runtime comments, and imports all describe the same ownership boundaries.
Broad stale-path searches need contextual review: historical records and explicit negative instructions can mention old paths for valid reasons.
Removing a compatibility shim after direct imports are migrated eliminates ambiguity about the canonical type location.
story_points: The code tree had already moved, but developers could still be guided toward files that no longer existed.
The cleanup preserved historical evidence while correcting current instructions and checked that tests/build still passed.
possible_angles: Why documentation drift is part of a refactor, not a separate polish task
How to review stale-path search results without rewriting history
What a compatibility shim is for—and when it is safe to remove

notes: Captured as raw source material after verification; no platform or publication decision made.
